Moreover, Allah the Exalted decrees on the Night of Decree what will occur during the year, and all of this is part of the completeness of His knowledge, the perfection of His wisdom, the precision of His preservation, and His care for His creation.

{5} {A command from Us}, meaning this wise matter is a command issued from Us. {Indeed, We have always been sending messengers}, to the messengers, and sending down books; the messengers convey the commands of the One who sends them and inform of His decrees.

{6} {As a mercy from your Lord}, meaning the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, the most excellent of which is the Qur'an, is a mercy from the Lord of the servants toward the servants. {7–8} {Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them}, meaning the Creator of that, its Manager, and the One who disposes of it as He wills. {If you are certain}, meaning if you have knowledge of this that yields certainty; then know that the Lord of the creatures is their true God. {10–16} {So watch}, meaning await punishment for them, for it has drawn near and its time has come {on the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. It will envelop the people}, meaning that smoke will encompass them, and it will be said to them: {This is a painful punishment}. The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of this smoke:

It was said: it is the smoke that envelops people and covers them when the Fire draws near to the criminals on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah threatened them with the punishment of the Day of Resurrection and commanded His Prophet to await that day for them. This meaning is supported by the fact that this is the Qur'an's method of threatening the disbelievers, patiently waiting for them, warning them with that day and its punishment, and consoling the Messenger and the believers with waiting for those who harmed them. It is further supported by His saying in this verse: {How can there be for them a reminder, when there came to them a clear messenger}, and this is said on the Day of Resurrection to the disbelievers when they seek to return to the world, and it is said: the time of return has passed.

It was said: the intended meaning is what befell the disbelievers of Quraysh when they refused to believe and were arrogant toward the truth, and the Prophet ﷺ supplicated against them, saying: "O Allah, help me against them with years like the years of Joseph." So Allah sent upon them a great famine, until they ate carrion and bones, and they began to see what was between the sky and the earth as if it were smoke, though it was not, and that was from the severity of hunger. It was said: the intended meaning is that this is one of the portents of the Hour, and that at the end of time there will be a smoke that seizes people's breaths, and it will afflict the believers with something like smoke.

The first view is the correct one. The verse admits the possibility that the intended meaning of: {So watch, the day the sky brings a visible smoke. If these verses are understood according to these two meanings, you will find nothing in the wording that prevents this; rather, you will find it fully consistent with both. This is what appears to me and what I prefer. And Allah knows best.

{51–53} This is the reward of those who are mindful of God, who guarded themselves against His wrath and punishment by abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience. When wrath and punishment were removed from them, God's good pleasure and great reward were established for them: ﴿in shade extended﴾, from the abundance of trees and fruits, ﴿and springs flowing﴾, with rivers running beneath them that they cause to gush forth abundantly, ﴿in gardens of bliss﴾. He attributed the gardens to bliss because everything they contain is bliss and complete joy from every aspect, with no disturbance or turbidity in any way. ﴿Their clothing will be of green silk, of fine brocade and thick silk﴾, that is, thick silk and fine silk, of what their souls desire. ﴿Facing one another﴾: in their hearts and faces, in perfect ease, tranquility, love, good companionship and praiseworthy manners.

{54} ﴿Thus﴾: complete bliss and perfect joy. ﴿And We will marry them to houris﴾, that is, women of beauty, whose loveliness and attractiveness are such that the eye is dazzled by their beauty, the mind is astonished by their loveliness, and the heart is captivated by their perfection. ﴿With wide, lovely eyes﴾, that is, large and beautiful eyes.

{55} ﴿They will call therein﴾, that is, in Paradise, ﴿for every fruit﴾: of what has a name in this world and of what has no name or equal in this world. Whatever kinds and varieties of fruit they ask for, it will be brought to them immediately, without weariness or hardship, secure from its ending, secure from its harm, secure from every disturbance, and secure from leaving it or from death.

{56} Hence He said: ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾, that is, there is no death in it at all. Had there been any death in it, He would not have excepted "the first death," which is the death of this world. Thus every beloved and desired thing is fulfilled for them. ﴿And He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.﴾

{58} ﴿Indeed, We have made it easy﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿in your tongue﴾, that is, We made it easy in your language, which is the most eloquent of tongues absolutely and the most noble, so its wording was made easy and its meaning was made easy. ﴿That they may be reminded﴾: of what benefits them so that they do it, and what harms them so that they abandon it.
